title: Development of a Novel Orthotopic Gastric Cancer Mouse Model
author: Kang, Maher, et al.
materials: Fresh or cryopreserved gastric cancer patient or xenograft tumor tissue.
Sterile cotton swabs (Med Vet International, CTA6STRLX10).
All procedures are performed in the biosafety cabinet.

steps.title: Prepare minced tumor matrix
steps.instruction: In a biosafety cabinet, wash the PDX tumor tissue with cold PBS, place on an ice‑packed petri dish and mince with sterile forceps and single‑edge razor blades into fragments <1 mm. Add 50 % Matrigel diluted in RPMI‑1640 (≈10–20 % of the tumor volume) to keep the tissue moist. Load the slurry through the plunger of a 5 mL syringe using forceps, expel all air, then transfer the bubble‑free matrix into a sterile 1 mL syringe fitted with an 18 G needle and keep on ice.

steps.title: Prepare soft tumor fragment
steps.instruction: In a biosafety cabinet, wash the tumor with cold PBS, place on ice, and cut into ~3 × 3 × 3 mm pieces with sterile forceps and razor blades. Select an optimal soft fragment and suspend it in 200 µL of 50 % Matrigel/RPMI‑1640. Keep on ice until transplantation.

steps.title: Anesthetize mouse and give analgesic
steps.instruction: Weigh an 8‑week‑old female NSG mouse, then inject intraperitoneally 100 mg/kg ketamine + 10 mg/kg xylazine. Immediately give ketoprofen 5 mg/kg IP as pre‑operative analgesia using a disposable 1 mL syringe.

steps.title: Pre‑operative preparation
steps.instruction: Place the mouse on a warming pad sized for microscopic surgery. Remove fur from the ventral abdomen and left flank (extend to dorsal midline if desired) with clippers, then clear loose hair with adhesive tape, dry gauze or gauze dampened with ethanol. Apply ophthalmic ointment to the eyes. Disinfect the skin with 70 % ethanol followed by chlorhexidine, using sterile swabs in outward‑expanding circles and a fresh swab for each agent. Cover the work area with a sterile disposable drape and position a sterile Invisishield Aperture Surgical Drape over the surgical site.

steps.title: Expose stomach
steps.instruction: With the mouse in dorsal recumbency under the microscope, make a 2.0 cm skin incision caudal and parallel to the most caudal rib using Von Graefe or Extra Fine Graefe forceps and iris scissors. Incise the underlying muscle, hold it with retractors, and expose the stomach. Hold the stomach with ring forceps and a moistened gauze to display the greater curvature.

steps.title: Create subserosal void
steps.instruction: Prepare a 31‑gauge insulin syringe on ice containing either 30–40 µL of 50 % Matrigel/RPMI‑1640 or sterile saline. Inject this volume into the subserosal layer of the stomach. Using Vannas Iridocapsulotomy scissors, incise the serosa 2–3 mm over the injection site to evacuate the injected solution; wipe any leaked fluid with sterile gauze or cotton swabs.

steps.title: Implant tumor material
steps.instruction: Widen the incision site with Micro‑Blunted Tip Dumont or Moria Iris forceps. Insert an 18 G needle into the created pocket and slowly inject up to 20 µL of the minced tumor matrix (or place the soft fragment with forceps as described in step 2). After injection, gently withdraw the needle and press the entry site with a sterile cotton swab for 20–30 s until it closes. Optionally cover the serosal incision with tissue adhesive or gelfoam.

steps.title: Close abdominal wall and skin
steps.instruction: Advance the stomach away from the opening. Close the abdominal wall with a 5‑0 or 6‑0 absorbable suture using micro needle holders. Apply 0.1 % bupivacaine to the skin edges, then close the skin with wound clips.

steps.title: Post‑operative recovery
steps.instruction: Place the mouse in lateral recumbency in a clean, warm cage. Record its body weight. Give sub‑cutaneous sterile saline warmed to 35–37 °C (1 mL per 25 g body weight) using a disposable 5 mL syringe. Keep the recovery cage on a heating pad set to 30–37 °C, allowing the mouse to move away from the heat once awake. Maintain the mouse in an individually ventilated cage once it is ambulatory.

steps.title: Euthanize and collect tumors
steps.instruction: Euthanize mice with 5 % CO₂ when body weight changes >20 % or when abnormal signs (ascites, reduced motility) appear. Using a surgical microscope, locate stomach and any metastatic tumors, photograph, and excise the masses.

steps.title: Process tissue for histology
steps.instruction: Slice each tumor mass to 1 mm thickness with a stainless‑steel tissue slicer matrix. Fix slices in 10 % neutral‑buffered formalin for 24 h at 4 °C. Embed in paraffin, then perform Hematoxylin & Eosin staining according to standard protocols. For immunohistochemistry, stain sections (collected at 3 weeks post‑surgery) with Ki‑67 antibody. Scan slides on a Hamamatsu NanoZoomer HT2.0 and examine morphology using NDPIView2 software.
